record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Describe and classify all surjective quadratic stochastic operators on the simplex S^{m-1} in every dimension m >= 5.

evidence.quote: In [5] and [28] a description of surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for m = 2, 3, 4 and classification of extreme points of the set of such operators are given.
Problem 14. Describe the set of all surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for any m ≥ 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ be an integer and let
$$S^{m-1}=\Big\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m : x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\Big\}$$
denote the standard $(m-1)$-simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(V x)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients $\{p_{ij,k}\}$ satisfy
$$p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0\quad\text{for all } i,j,k,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all } i,j.$$
Such an operator $V$ is called surjective if $V(S^{m-1})=S^{m-1}$.

For each $m\ge 5$, give a complete description and classification of all surjective quadratic stochastic operators on $S^{m-1}$, and describe the extreme points of the convex set of such operators.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably Bartoszek–Pułka, "On the surjectivity of quadratic stochastic operators acting on the simplex," 2016, and related papers by Mukhamedov and coauthors) gives a structural characterization of surjective QSOs in arbitrary dimension: a QSO on $S^{m-1}$ is surjective if and only if it can be written as a composition involving a permutation and a Lotka–Volterra-type QSO, and such operators are necessarily bijective. However, an explicit complete classification and a full description of the extreme points of the surjective set for general $m\ge 5$ does not appear to have been fully achieved, so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the surjectivity of quadratic stochastic operators acting on the simplex
status_evidence.snippet: A QSO is a surjection of the simplex if and only if it is bijective; surjective QSOs are characterized via a permutation matrix and a Lotka–Volterra QSO.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a structural characterization of surjective QSOs in arbitrary dimension.

status_evidence.title: A class of bijective Lotka–Volterra operators and its application
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a class of Lotka–Volterra QSOs that are bijective on the simplex, extending the structural understanding of surjective QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Further structural results on bijective/surjective QSOs in higher dimensions, but not a full extreme-point classification.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic operators corresponding to permutations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies QSOs associated with permutations, related to the description of surjective/bijective QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research on the description problem indicates partial progress for general m.
